actions.text: Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. Ordered to be reported without amendment favorably.
Committee on Energy and Natural Resources Subcommittee on Energy. Hearings held. With printed Hearing: S.Hrg. 119-366.
Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.

dimensions.assessment: Affects electric generation project developers, transmission providers, independent system operators, and regional transmission organizations.
dimensions.evidence: authorize transmission providers to submit proposals to the Commission to adjust the interconnection queue

dimensions.assessment: Alters the prioritization and approval structure for electricity generation interconnection requests to favor dispatchable power.
dimensions.evidence: prioritize new dispatchable power projects that will improve grid reliability and resource adequacy by assigning those projects higher positions

dimensions.assessment: The source does not mention explicit federal spending or revenue changes.
Requires FERC to issue regulations and review transmission provider proposals within strict 60-day windows.
dimensions.evidence: the Commission shall initiate a rulemaking--(1) to address the inefficiencies and ineffectiveness of existing procedures

dimensions.assessment: Requires a final rule within 180 days and mandates periodic reviews by FERC at least once every 5 years.
dimensions.evidence: Not less frequently than once every 5 years, the Commission shall review and, if necessary, update the regulations

missing_information: Specific estimates of administrative costs for FERC or transmission providers
Number of generation projects that would receive priority queuing
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates a FERC rulemaking to allow transmission providers to prioritize dispatchable power projects in interconnection queues to address grid reliability.
